verdict.rationale: The IRS documents Modernized e-File (MeF) as an XML system-to-system rail and IRIS Application to Application (A2A) as a machine intake for information returns gated by a Transmitter Control Code. It also publishes the Authorized e-File Provider enrollment path, including approval of up to 45 days and fingerprinting, plus an Assurance Testing System for transmitters. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of enrollment and transmission, and publicly downloadable interface definitions (schemas and WSDLs are registration-gated).

support.subject: As a legal-ops lead, a documented system-to-system channel exists for software to transact with the service (system accounts, transmitter programs, batch providers), with the enrollment path published

citations.quote: MeF uses the widely accepted Extensible Markup Language (XML) format.
IRIS "receives information through two intake channels: IRIS Taxpayer Portal/UI and IRIS Application to Application (A2A)"
it can take up to 45 days from the date of submission for the IRS to approve your e-file application

Transmitters, software developers, and state agencies are encouraged to review their implementations and complete any necessary changes in ATS prior to the Production deployment to avoid service disruptions.
